thread:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: hotpath GPU pool 'gpupool-1' queue depth spiking to 12k, sustained 429s across tier 'prod-high'. autocancel: false :rotating_light:
maya: seeing the pages. I’m on it. starting a quick triage — queue and autoscale logs first.
jamal: adding context — we deployed a routing change ~20m ago that moved more traffic to the hotpath; autoscale config has a hard cap at 16 nodes currently.
linh: pulling autoscale logs now. `autoscaler:policy=hotpath` shows repeated scale attempts failing with `launch_timeout` and `scale_up_limit_reached`. also token-bucket drops spiking in rate-policy.
alex: customers complaining in support — how bad is impact? are top-tier customers getting 429s?
csm_evan: CSM notes: NimbleHR and AtlasAI have reported 15-30% request failures since ~10:32 UTC. they're seeing streaming disconnects and 429s. escalating.
ryan_oncall: paging customers + notifying sales ops. tagging legal if SLA hit.
maya: quick check: `rqueues inspect gpupool-1 --depth` shows backlog ~11.8k, processing rate smeared. tokens emitted per sec < expected. looks like token-bucket refill is bottlenecking routing -> leads to immediate 429s.
jamal: that jives with the rate-policy patch from yesterday. config snippet I pulled:```yaml
tier: prod-high
max_tokens_per_sec: 1200
burst_capacity: 500
strict_token_enforcement: true
```
refill math doesn't match current aggregate qps after routing change.
linh: also autoscaler target_idle_pct tuned low (10%) + aggressive cooldown. with sustained surge and failed launches we never reach new desired. nodes at 16 = cap.
maya: immediate mitigations proposed:
- relax token enforcement: set `strict_token_enforcement: false` for prod-high
- bump burst_capacity 500 -> 2500 temporarily
- increase autoscale cap 16 -> 32 and trigger manual scale to 24 now
- route a subset of traffic to gpupool-2 (fallback region) until stable
who can do each?
jamal: I can flip the rate-policy flags (will open a config change). applying now.
linh: I’ll raise autoscale cap and kick manual scale. doing `infractl pools update gpupool-1 --max-nodes=32` then `infractl pools scale gpupool-1 --desired=24`. executing.
maya: I'll open route change. `routerctl route weight set prod-high gpupool-1=0.75 gpupool-2=0.25` to shed 25% to fallback.
csm_evan: want to loop customers — I’ll post a quick status to NimbleHR and AtlasAI with ETA and mitigation.
incident-bot: config-change:jamal applied rate-policy update at 1967653330 (burst_capacity: 2500, strict_token_enforcement: false).
jamal: done — committed and rolled to edge config, should take ~20s to propagate.
linh: infractl returned success. desired=24, nodes provisioning. launcher logs show queued instances started.
maya: metrics check: p95 latency stable, 429 rate starting to drop from 18% -> 8% after config flip + route change. queue depth decreasing to 6.1k. continuing to watch. :eyes:
ryan_oncall: CS notified. they acknowledged the temporary mitigation, asked for updates every 30m.
ajex: (typo) sorry — alex: thanks. please call out when 429s < 1% for 10m and we can clear SEV.
jamal: autoscaler reported 3 nodes failed to bootstrap due to instance limit in region; we've hit a cloud quota. requesting temporary quota bump now. opened cloud ticket INC-84012.
linh: manually started alternate instance types in same AZ to speed up capacity while cloud ops completes quota bump.
maya: 429s now at 1.8% over last 5m, queue depth 900, processing throughput normalizing.
incident-bot: severity bumped to SEV2 -> SEV3 candidate if steady for 15m.
csm_evan: customers updated: NimbleHR accepted the mitigation; AtlasAI asked for postmortem and SLA credit estimate.
ryan_oncall: handoff note for next oncall: monitor gpupool-1, confirm cloud quota ticket resolution, coordinate postmortem. owner: maya.
maya: acknowledged handoff. starting a short runbook to capture timeline:```text
- 1967653320: routing change -> surge
- 1967653325: pages start
- 1967653330: rate-policy relaxed
- 1967653340: routing weight shift
- 1967653360: manual scale and alt instances
- 1967653380: 429s < 2% and stabilizing
```
jamal: postmortem owners: eng-runtime (jamal), eng-infra (linh), SRE (maya). will include regression test for rate-policy changes and autoscale cap alarms.
linh: follow-ups: add autoscale safety override to bypass region quota on emergency, and add preflight check when applying large routing shifts.
maya: confirming we will revert temp changes only after stable 1% 429 for 30m, and then roll back `burst_capacity` & `strict_token_enforcement` after postmortem.
incident-bot: automated note posted to #incidents-log. ticket created: RED-INC-2026-1498.
ryan_oncall: leaving final note: handover to day team at 08:00 UTC, Maya to coordinate postmortem and customer comms. thanks team. :clap:
